findings.title: Commit 31eeeb2f falsely reported boredom goal[6] as completed when it had already failed
findings.analysis: Commit 31eeeb2f (2026-05-26 12:48:38 PDT = 19:48:38 UTC) updated current_focus to state: 'Boredom firing all 7 goals cleanly: goal[3] 18:09Z, goal[4] 18:39Z, goal[5] 19:09Z, goal[6] 19:39Z all completed.' However, boredom goal[6] (probe-untraversed-edge) submitted at 19:39:30 UTC FAILED at 19:44:29 UTC with exit-code, 4 minutes before the commit was authored. Commit b38c8776 (19:51 UTC, 3 minutes later) then acknowledged the failure and replaced goal[6]. The false claim persisted for 12 minutes across two commits before being corrected in 346a0ca0 (20:00 UTC).

findings.title: Container src/engine.ts (487 lines, May 25) does not match deployed dist/engine.js (compiled May 26 19:43) — source/dist split deployment pattern
findings.analysis: The substrate uses a split deployment pattern where src/ files in the container are not always up to date, but dist/ compiled files are what actually runs. Container /vessels/ias-executor-ts/src/engine.ts is 487 lines with mtime May 25 02:34 UTC. The repo's current engine.ts (at 49bfb43) is 514 lines. However, dist/engine.js was recompiled at 2026-05-26 19:43:58 UTC and does contain lifecycle:gap:classified at lines 78 and 125. This means the 31eeeb2f deployment claim 'Deployed to all 7 vessel node_modules' is CORRECT for gap:classified — it's in the running dist. However, the src/ directory mismatch means a developer running `wc -l /vessels/ias-executor-ts/src/engine.ts` would get incorrect information about the deployed version. This creates an audit verification trap: checking src lines gives stale answers.

evidence.gap_classified_in_src: docker exec substrate-live grep -n 'gap:classified' /vessels/ias-executor-ts/src/engine.ts → no output (src not updated)
